ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AC = BC = 13$. Place $\triangle ABC$ in the Cartesian coordinate system, with the coordinates of points A and B being $(2, 0)$ and $(12, 0)$, respectively. Translate $\triangle ABC$ along the x-axis to the left such that point C lies on the line $y = -x + 8$. What is the distance of this translation of $\triangle ABC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct CD $\perp$ x-axis at point D, as shown in the figure.\\
Since the coordinates of points A and B are respectively (2, 0) and (12, 0), and AC=BC=13,\\
it follows that AD=BD=$\frac{1}{2}$AB=5,\\
hence CD=$\sqrt{AC^{2}-AD^{2}}=12$.\\
Therefore, the coordinates of point C are (7, 12).\\
When y=12, we have 12=$-x+8$,\\
solving this gives: x=$-4$,\\
thus, the coordinates of point C after translation are ($-4$, 12).\\
Therefore, $\triangle ABC$ is translated 7-(-4)=\boxed{11} units length to the left along the x-axis.

method.method_draft: Use the visible structure that A and B are on the x-axis and C is above them in an isosceles triangle. From the text read A=(2,0), B=(12,0), and AC=BC=13. Since AC=BC, drop the altitude from C to the x-axis; in an isosceles triangle this altitude hits the midpoint of AB, so the foot has x-coordinate 7 and each half of AB is 5. Use the right triangle with hypotenuse 13 and leg 5 to get the height CD=12, so C=(7,12). A translation along the x-axis preserves C's y-coordinate, so the translated point C must have y=12. Substitute into the visually labeled/text-given line y=-x+8: 12=-x+8, giving x=-4. The horizontal translation distance is from initial x=7 to final x=-4, hence 11 units left.

thus, the coordinates of point C after translation are ($-4$, 12).\\
Therefore, $\triangle ABC$ is translated 7-(-4)=\boxed{11} units length to the left along the x-axis.
